strategy.summary: Reproduce gh-20021 by building SciPy at the buggy commit 673a15da1366 and running the added test test_instability_gh20021 in scipy/stats/tests/test_morestats.py. The test calls stats.boxcox_llf(1e-8, [2003, 1950, 1997, 2000, 2009]) and asserts assert_allclose against -15.32401272869016598. Success is the transition: the test fails on the buggy revision and passes on the fixed revision that factors out the 1/lmb term (logvar = _log_var(logx) - 2*log(abs(lmb))). Numpy and matplotlib versions are unconstrained by documentation, so the environment is chosen by us and stated as such.

pinned_because: No documented numpy or matplotlib constraint exists in the evidence; numpy is left unpinned and the choice is ours, so any numpy release that builds against this SciPy revision is acceptable.
matplotlib is not needed: it is only imported by the PR's standalone reproduction script, not by the pytest test, so it is omitted.
Build tooling versions are era-inferred from the SciPy build system of that period, not documented in the evidence; mpmath is not needed by the test itself because the reference value is hard-coded.

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/stats/tests/test_morestats.py::TestBoxcox::test_instability_gh20021 (added after test_gh_6873; class name inferred from neighbouring tests)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 673a15da1366 the test fails at assert_allclose(llf, -15.32401272869016598) because the computed llf differs from the reference by more than the default rtol of 1e-7; on the fixed revision the same test passes with the same assertion and the same input.
strategy.numerical_probe: Compare stats.boxcox_llf(1e-8, data) against -15.32401272869016598 using assert_allclose default tolerances on both revisions; the relative gap is what decides the transition.
risks: The buggy output is not in the evidence, so it is unknown whether the discrepancy exceeds the default rtol of 1e-7; if it does not, the test will not transition and the reproduction is not confirmed.

The defect is an accuracy loss from cancellation near lambda=0, so its size can depend on the floating-point behaviour of numpy's log and on the BLAS/libm of the platform; it may appear on some architectures and not others, which is not established here.
The reference value has 20 significant digits, beyond float64 precision; the test relies on assert_allclose tolerance, not exact digits.
The reviewer noted that mpmath.mp.dps=100 gave a different value in discussion, so the reference itself carries uncertainty of unknown size.
The integer literal data and the float64 dtype of the computation are not stated; the defect's dtype dependence cannot be grounded.
No sanitiser or special threading is assumed; if the defect only appears under a specific compiler or flag set the transition may fail on a standard build.
PR date is unknown, so the era of numpy and build tooling is inferred and not verified.

oracle.why: The test compares against a hard-coded high-precision reference with the library default tolerance, so the pass/fail boundary is the default relative tolerance.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The assertion sees the buggy boxcox_llf value, which carries cancellation error from subtracting the 1/lmb offset near lambda=1e-8; if that error exceeds relative 1e-7 against -15.32401272869016598, assert_allclose raises AssertionError. Magnitude not given in evidence.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the 1/lmb term factored out (logvar = _log_var(logx) - 2*log(abs(lmb))), the computed value is expected to match the reference within rtol 1e-7, so assert_allclose passes; this is the PR's claim and is not independently verified in the evidence.
